scope: Safe classroom experiment concepts only. These are software teaching lenses, not real-world laboratory instructions.

experiments.title: States of matter at a glance
experiments.focus: Compare solid, liquid and gas using the virtual model.
student_observations: Ice keeps its shape.
Water takes the shape of the container.
Air expands to fill space.
experiments.teacher_note: Use it as a visual classification activity.

experiments.title: What a solution looks like
experiments.focus: Observe a homogeneous mixture in the classroom model.
student_observations: The solid becomes invisible in the liquid.
The mixture stays uniform.
The solute is still present even when not visible.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the explanation particle-level and visual only.

experiments.title: Mixtures and simple sorting
experiments.focus: Discuss visible differences between a dissolved sample and an insoluble mixture.
student_observations: Sand remains separate.
The mixture is not uniform.
Some materials do not dissolve in water.
experiments.teacher_note: Link the activity to the idea of separation methods without giving a lab procedure.

experiments.title: Solvent and solute roles
experiments.focus: Identify the solvent and the solute in the model solution.
student_observations: Water is the solvent.
Salt is the solute.
The particles become distributed in the liquid.
experiments.teacher_note: Ask students to explain the difference before showing the guide text.

experiments.title: A saturation idea
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea of a limit to dissolving under a chosen condition.
student_observations: Extra solid can remain at the bottom.
The solution can stop becoming more concentrated.
The model needs a stated temperature.
experiments.teacher_note: Describe it as a concept, not a measured curve.

experiments.title: Heating and cooling as physical changes
experiments.focus: Connect heating with melting and boiling at a high level.
student_observations: Heating changes the state.
The substance stays water.
Temperature helps explain what happens.
experiments.teacher_note: Use the model to compare observations and explanations.

experiments.title: Magnesium combustion · white-light observation model
experiments.focus: Recognise the qualitative observations associated with magnesium reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.
student_observations: A brilliant white light is shown briefly in the virtual scene.
The model displays a white solid product labelled magnesium oxide (MgO).
The displayed product amount is illustrative, not a calculated yield.
experiments.teacher_note: Observation-only virtual demonstration. It contains no ignition method, real-world apparatus setup, quantities for practice or procedural steps. The periodic-table magnesium sample remains a read-only visual reference.

experiments.title: Conservation in a closed model
experiments.focus: Show that matter is not lost when a process only rearranges particles.
student_observations: The sample changes appearance.
The total amount in the model stays accounted for.
A model can simplify reality without breaking the idea.

experiments.title: Classifying familiar materials
experiments.focus: Compare compounds, mixtures and gases in a classroom-safe way.
student_observations: Air is a mixture.
Carbon dioxide is a compound.
Sand is a solid material used for mixture examples.
experiments.teacher_note: This is a discussion activity with visual support.

experiments.title: Reviewing a clear solution
experiments.focus: Revisit the dissolved-state model and explain why the liquid stays clear.
student_observations: The solution can remain transparent.
Dissolved particles are too small to see individually.
The model uses a simplified timescale.
experiments.teacher_note: Great as a short recap before a test or quiz.

experiments.title: Particles, energy and state
experiments.focus: Link particle motion to the visible state of matter.
student_observations: Heating increases motion in the model.
Cooling can reverse the change.
Physical changes are not chemical reactions.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect it to biology and Earth science where helpful.

experiments.title: Glucose and starch as study examples
experiments.focus: Compare a small molecule with a polymeric carbohydrate.
student_observations: Glucose is a small molecular formula.
Starch has repeating units.
The two are used differently in living systems.
experiments.teacher_note: Stay at the classroom explanation level.

experiments.title: Carbon dioxide in science systems
experiments.focus: Discuss how chemistry links to the carbon cycle and the water cycle.
student_observations: Carbon dioxide is part of the atmosphere.
Water appears in many system models.
Some substances are mixtures rather than single compounds.

experiments.title: What a scientific model can and cannot show
experiments.focus: Evaluate the simulation as a model and identify its assumptions.
student_observations: The model simplifies reality.
Some values are marked unverified or derived.
A model is useful even when it is not complete.
experiments.teacher_note: Good for revision before higher secondary planning.

experiments.title: Pathway-aware lesson planning
experiments.focus: Show why Senior 2 content must match the student's exact pathway.
student_observations: Not all students follow the same official map.
The app can show safe concepts across pathways.
The final syllabus still needs confirmation.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this to avoid mixing General Secondary and Baccalaureate assumptions.

experiments.title: Safe review of classroom chemistry concepts
experiments.focus: Reinforce safe, non-hazardous classroom concepts before exam revision.
student_observations: Dissolution remains a physical change.
Reference entries can still teach chemistry.
Safety and evidence matter together.
experiments.teacher_note: This is a recap lesson, not a lab procedure guide.
